attrs.class: alt-font fw-600 text-dark-gray w-90 sm-w-100 mx-auto mb-15px

children: When direction is clear, design reviews become sharper, faster, and more useful.
A useful strategy brief answers the questions design usually inherits too late.

It should explain the business objective, who the piece is trying to move, what must be understood in a few seconds, and where the visual system can flex without losing recognition. That turns subjective feedback into decisions the whole team can defend.
Direction should reduce noise, not add more documents.

The best systems are easy to use. They translate into layout logic, content priorities, and repeatable asset decisions the team can apply in social posts, presentations, launch campaigns, and day-to-day marketing.
Consistency grows when teams know what should never change.

That usually means clarifying a few non-negotiables: tone, typographic behavior, spacing rhythm, key color usage, and the visual cues that make the brand recognizable even in smaller, faster deliverables.
